newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen up as rate hike fears fade on Tokai.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen up as rate hike fears fade on Tokai.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures extended gains on Friday as lingering rate hike fears were erased by fresh corporate woes in Japan, dealers said.
"If there were still doubts of an imminent rate hike in Japan, the Tokai Kogyo news should have erased them," said a dealer with a European institution.
"How can BOJ (Bank of Japan) raise rates when problems after problems seem to be surfacing," he added.
Japanese construction firm Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd, with a debt of 511 billion yen, said on Friday it had made an application for court protection from creditors under Japanese bankruptcy laws.
The news sent most construction stocks tumbling in Tokyo and weighed on Japan's economic outlook, dealers said.
"There was a sell-out in Nikkei, especially after a sell-off in the construction sector in Tokyo following the Tokai Kogyo news," said a dealer with a local institution.
At 1115 GMT, March Euroyen futures were around 99.03 against their IMM close at 98.99 on Thursday. Volume was 19,085 lots.
The JGB bulls continued their run as September broke key resistance of 125.00 to end at 125.15, up 0.29.
Dealers said investors' interest continued to stream into JGBs given the weak stock market.
Both JGBS and Euroyen futures were likely to stay firm amid these corporate troubles in Japan, they said.

Eurodollar futures were stable, deriving no further inspiration from Thursday's U.S. June non-farm payrolls which grew by 217,000 new jobs and the jump in June unemployment by 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent in May.
"The weak data reinforced belief the U.S. rates will remain stable for sometime," said the dealer with a local institution. September ended at 94.200 against its IMM close at 94.200 on 6,680 lots.
